chunks: 1. Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿĪsā ibn Hishām, from al-Khaḍir ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥakīm, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about the day concerning which there is doubt. The people claim that whoever fasts it is like one who broke the fast for a day of the month of Ramadan. He said: They have lied. If it is from the month of Ramadan, then it is a day to which he was granted success; and if it is from other than it, then it is like the past days.
2. From him, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about the day concerning which there is doubt in relation to the month of Ramadan, and it is not known whether it is from Shaʿbān or from Ramadan, and he fasted it from the month of Ramadan. He said: It is a day to which he was granted success, and there is no qaḍāʾ upon him.
3. From him, from Aḥmad, from Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ṣahbān, from Muḥammad ibn Bakr ibn Janāḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Shajarah, from Bashīr al-Nabbāl, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about fasting the Day of Doubt, and he said: Fast it; if it is from Shaʿbān, it will be supererogatory, and if it is from the month of Ramadan, then it is a day to which you were granted success.
4. Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ḥamzah ibn Yaʿlā, from Zakariyyā ibn Ādam, from al-Kāhilī, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the day of Shaʿbān concerning which there is doubt. He said: That I fast a day from Shaʿbān is more beloved to me than that I break the fast for a day from the month of Ramadan.
5. From him, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ṣahbān, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Ribāṭ, from Saʿīd al-Aʿraj, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I fasted the day concerning which there is doubt, and it turned out to be from the month of Ramadan. Shall I make it up? He said: No. It is a day to which you were granted success.
6. As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim and Abī Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who fasts the day concerning which there is doubt as part of Ramadan, he said: Its qaḍāʾ is upon him. If that is so, then the proper way concerning this report is one of two things: either that we interpret it as a kind of taqiyyah, because it agrees with the doctrine of some of the ʿāmmah; or that we interpret it concerning one who fasted on the basis that it was from the month of Ramadan. For whenever the matter is like that, its qaḍāʾ becomes obligatory upon him, because he fasted that which it is not permissible for him to fast. Rather, it is only allowed for him to fast this day on the basis that it is from Shaʿbān, as we have clarified. And what has preceded indicates that whenever he fasts with the intention of Shaʿbān, qaḍāʾ is not binding upon him, in addition to what has already passed.
7. What Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man fasted a day while not knowing whether this was from the month of Ramadan or from other than it. Then some people came and testified that it had been from the month of Ramadan, and some of the people among us said that it does not count. He said: Yes, it does count. I said: They said, “You fasted while you did not know whether this was from the month of Ramadan or from other than it.” He said: Yes, so count it, for it is only something to which Allah granted you success. The Day of Doubt is only fasted as part of Shaʿbān, and you must not fast it as part of the month of Ramadan, because it has been prohibited for a person to single himself out for fasting on the Day of Doubt. Rather, he intends from the night that he is fasting as part of Shaʿbān; then if it is from the month of Ramadan, it suffices for him for it by the grace of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and by what He has expanded for His servants. Were it not for that, the people would perish.
8. As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jaʿfar al-Azdī, from Qutaybah al-Aʿshā, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade fasting on six days: the two ʿĪds, the days of al-Tashrīq, and the day concerning which there is doubt as part of the month of Ramadan.
9. From him, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī and others, from ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿAmr, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I have bound myself that I will fast until al-Qāʾim عجل الله تعالى فرجه rises. He said: Do not fast while travelling, nor on the two ʿĪds, nor on the days of al-Tashrīq, nor on the day concerning which there is doubt. As for what runs along the line of these two reports from the reports that include the prohibition of fasting the Day of Doubt, then the proper view is that it is not permissible to fast this day on the basis that it is from Ramadan, even though fasting it is permissible on the basis that it is from Shaʿbān. We have already clarified what indicates that, and what further clarifies it is:

10. What Abū al-Ḥasan Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Walīd narrated from his father, from al-Ṣaffār, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad al-Qāshānī, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad Kāsūlā, from Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd al-Shādhakawnī, from ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from Muḥammad ibn Shihāb al-Zuhrī, who said:

I heard ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام saying: The Day of Doubt—we were commanded to fast it and we were forbidden from it. We were commanded that a person fast it on the basis that it is from Shaʿbān, and we were forbidden from fasting it on the basis that it is from the month of Ramadan while he has not seen the الهلال.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precaution in expression due to opposing conditions
key_terms.الْهِلَالَ: the crescent whose sighting establishes the month
key_terms.بِنِيَّةِ شَعْبَانَ: with the intention that the fast is for Shaʿbān
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: the month preceding Ramadan, from which the intention for this fast should be made
key_terms.وُفِّقَ لَهُ: granted divine success to perform it correctly
key_terms.يَوْمُ الشَّكِّ: the day whose status is uncertain between Shaʿbān and Ramadan

ai.seo_question: Can Yawm al-Shakk be fasted, and does it count for Ramadan if it later turns out to be from Ramadan?
ai.summary: These narrations discuss the legal ruling of fasting Yawm al-Shakk, the day when it is uncertain whether the month is Shaʿbān or Ramadan. They indicate that fasting it is valid if intended as a fast of Shaʿbān, and if it later proves to be from Ramadan, it suffices and does not require qaḍāʾ. The prohibition applies to fasting it specifically with the assumption that it is definitely from Ramadan before confirmation of the crescent.
